title: Thor in a wedding dress
premise: A giant steals Thor's hammer and demands Freyja as his bride, so Thor goes in disguise.

title: How Loki became the mother of a horse
premise: A builder's deal to wall Asgard goes wrong, and Loki fixes it in the strangest way possible.

title: The mead of poetry
premise: Odin steals the drink that makes you a poet, and bad poetry gets a very specific origin.

title: The god killed by a plant
premise: Everything in creation swears not to harm Baldr, except one plant nobody thought to ask.

title: How Anansi bought all the world's stories
source: Akan oral tradition; recorded in R. S. Rattray, Akan-Ashanti Folk-Tales (1930)
premise: A spider buys every story from the sky god by capturing four 'impossible' creatures.

title: Anansi tries to hide all the wisdom
premise: Anansi collects all the wisdom in the world into one pot, then gets outsmarted by his own son.

title: Why the tortoise's shell is cracked
source: Igbo folktale; retold in Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart (1958)
premise: Tortoise renames himself 'All of You' to steal a feast from the birds in the sky.

title: Why the sun and moon live in the sky
source: Efik folktale; recorded in Elphinstone Dayrell, Folk Stories from Southern Nigeria (1910)
premise: The sun and moon invite the water to visit their house. It does not go well for the house.

title: Eshu's two-coloured hat
premise: A trickster walks between two best friends in a hat that is red on one side and white on the other.

title: The god who created humans while drunk
premise: Obatala is given the job of shaping humans, then discovers palm wine halfway through.

title: How beer saved humanity
source: The Book of the Heavenly Cow
premise: Ra sends a goddess to wipe out humanity, then changes his mind and has to trick her with red-dyed beer.

title: The divine court case decided by lettuce
source: The Contendings of Horus and Set (Papyrus Chester Beatty I)
premise: Two gods fight for the throne for 80 years in a trial full of very bad behaviour (keep it ad-friendly).

title: The sun goddess who sulked in a cave
premise: The sun hides in a cave and the gods get her out with a mirror, a rooster and a dance party.

title: Getting an eight-headed dragon drunk
premise: A banished storm god defeats a giant serpent with eight bowls of very strong sake.

title: The fisherman who opened the box
source: Urashima Taro legend; earliest version in Nihon Shoki (720)
premise: A fisherman visits an undersea palace for three days and is told one thing: don't open the box.

title: Momotaro's original origin
premise: Before he was born from a peach, an older version had a very different explanation for the baby.

title: Kachi-kachi Yama: the darkest Japanese fairy tale
premise: A rabbit takes revenge on a tanuki in increasingly creative ways (hint at the darkness, don't show it).

title: The first barbecue scam
premise: Prometheus tricks Zeus into choosing bones wrapped in fat, and humanity gets the good meat forever.

title: Pandora never had a box
premise: It was a jar, and the thing left inside it is the most confusing part of the story.

title: Medusa's original story
source: Hesiod, Theogony; Ovid, Metamorphoses Book IV
premise: The earliest and later versions of Medusa disagree about who she was and why she was cursed.

title: The man who handcuffed Death
premise: Before the boulder, Sisyphus chained up Death himself, and nobody could die.

title: The worst dinner party in history
premise: A king tests whether the gods are all-knowing in the worst possible way.

title: Cinderella's stepsisters cut off their own toes
premise: No fairy godmother, a magic tree, a lot of shoe-related self-harm, and revenge birds.

title: The Little Mermaid's real ending
source: Hans Christian Andersen, Den lille Havfrue (1837)
premise: Every step hurts like knives, the prince marries someone else, and the ending is not a wedding.

title: Sleeping Beauty's original version
source: Giambattista Basile, Sun, Moon, and Talia (Pentamerone, 1634)
premise: The oldest version is so dark the later ones quietly rewrote it (hint only, keep it ad-friendly).

title: Snow White's queen tried three times
premise: A lace, a comb and an apple, and the wedding ends with very hot iron shoes.

title: The Frog Prince was never kissed
source: Grimm, The Frog King, or Iron Henry (KHM 1)
premise: The princess breaks the spell by throwing the frog at a wall. And who is Iron Henry?

title: The Pied Piper was (maybe) real
source: Hamelin town records (1384 entry); Grimm, Deutsche Sagen
premise: A German town's records say 130 children left in 1284. Historians still argue about why.

title: The town that danced itself to exhaustion
source: Strasbourg city records, 1518; John Waller, A Time to Dance, a Time to Die (2008)
premise: Hundreds of people dance for days, and the authorities' solution is to hire a band.

title: The war Australia lost to birds
premise: Soldiers with machine guns versus 20,000 emus. Guess who won.
